However, the stormwater volumes were too large for the basin to meaningfully reduce flows. As a result, the 100-year alternative was not pursued further, and a 25-year culvert improvement alternative was developed. The existing 10-foot by 6-foot box culvert under SR 341 (Occidental Grade) is undersized and flow overtops the roadway in both the 25-year and 100-year storm events. Because SR 342 is classified by NDOT as a Major Collector, the culvert crossing may be designed for the 25-year event. To pass the 25- year storm without overtopping the roadway, the existing culvert would be upgraded to a 10-foot by 8- foot box culvert. Lyon County does not typically conduct plan reviews or inspections for fire code compliance, except in limited circumstances involving development located outside the jurisdictional boundaries of local fire protection districts. As a result, the adoption of the updated fire code provisions does not appear likely to create additional staffing requirements, operational burdens, or ongoing fiscal obligations for the County. The primary anticipated cost to the County is the acquisition of the updated IFC code books and related reference materials necessary to satisfy statutory requirements for public inspection. Executive Summary This report provides the Board of County Commissioners with a comprehensive update on code enforcement actions taken with respect to the property located at [address redacted], Dayton, Nevada (Assessor's Parcel Number 016-151-14). Over a period of approximately ten months, Lyon County Code Enforcement Division, in collaboration with multiple partner agencies, successfully facilitated the complete remediation and cleanup of the subject property. The operation proceeded lawfully, safely, and in full accordance with the coordinated plan developed by participating agencies.

Background In June 2025, the Lyon County Code Enforcement Division initiated formal contact with the owners of Parcel 016-151-14 regarding conditions identified on the subject property that posed public health risks, safety hazards, and environmental concerns, and which had generated increasing community complaints. The Division issued written correspondence to the property owner notifying them of the situation and requesting their engagement in developing a coordinated and lawful course of action. That initial correspondence marked the beginning of an extensive ten-month collaborative effort between Lyon County Code Enforcement and the property ownership group. Notice to Vacate Operations On Thursday, April 16, 2026, the Lyon County Code Enforcement Officer, assisted by deputies from the Lyon County Sheriff's Office, conducted formal posting and personal service of Notices to Vacate throughout the subject property. Prior to the issuance of notices, the property owner had executed a trespass order through the Lyon County Sheriff's Office, which authorized the condensed 48-hour notice period afforded to occupants to vacate the premises in accordance with applicable legal requirements. Upon expiration of the notice period at 2:00 p.m. on Saturday, April 18, 2026, deputies from the Lyon County Sheriff's Office responded to the site. That creates a potential loophole. A data center could be approved while the most consequential offsite infrastructure—high-voltage transmission lines, utility substations, and easements—is deferred or processed separately. It is phased and cumulative. However, the draft permits review no more frequently than every five years. That is too infrequent for rapidly changing equipment, battery disposal costs, inflation, and site conditions.
